cards.title: Defining a search problem
cards.hook: Before an agent can search, we must describe the world as states, actions and costs.
cards.visual:
ComponentRomania example
State space20 cities
Initial stateArad
Goal state + goal testBucharest; goal_fun(s) = 1 if s = Bucharest
ACTIONS(s)drive to a connected city
RESULT(s,a)the city you arrive in
Action costroad distance, e.g. cost(A,S) = 140
formula: a fixed sequence of actions from start to goal
the one with the least path cost (e.g. 418 km, not 450 or 733)
example: Two solutions Arad→Bucharest: blue A-S-F-B = 140+99+211 = 450; green A-T-L-M-D-C-P-B = 733.
cards.memory: SIGAT-C: States, Initial, Goal, Actions, Transition, Cost.
cards.trap: The goal TEST is part of the problem; the PATH (sequence of actions) is the solution, not a single state.

cards.title: Frontier, tree search and graph search
cards.hook: Search grows a tree from the start state; the frontier is the to-do list of leaves.
cards.visual:
Tree searchGraph search
Remembers explored states?NoYes (explored set)
Repeated statesPossible (e.g. Arad→Sibiu→Arad)Never re-expanded
Add child if…alwaysnot in frontier or explored
formula: set of leaf nodes = candidates to expand
apply ACTIONS + RESULT to create children, connect them to n
which frontier node to pick next
example: Expand Arad → children Sibiu, Timișoara, Zerind join the frontier.
Expand Sibiu in TREE search → Arad appears again as a child (repeated state).
cards.memory: Tree search has amnesia; graph search keeps a diary (explored set).
cards.trap: In the lecture pseudocode the goal test for tree/graph search, UCS and A* happens when a node is SELECTED for expansion, but the BFS/DFS code tests when a child is GENERATED.

cards.title: BFS vs DFS (uninformed search)
cards.hook: Blind searches use no knowledge of where the goal is.
cards.visual:
BFSDFS
FrontierFIFO queueLIFO stack
Expandsshallowest nodedeepest node
Complete?Yes*No
Cost-optimal?Yes (unit costs: fewest actions)No
TimeO(b^d)O(b^m)
SpaceO(b^d)O(bm)
example: Binary tree A(B(D,E),C(F,G)): BFS order A, B, C, D, E, F, G.
DFS with goal M: A, B, D, H, I, E, J, K, C, F, L, M.
cards.memory: BFS = Breadth = Bread queue (first in line served first). DFS = Dive deep, stack of plates.
cards.trap: DFS uses little memory but returns the FIRST solution it finds, even if it's expensive.

cards.title: Uniform-cost search (UCS)
cards.hook: UCS always grows the cheapest path so far, like water spreading evenly.
cards.visual:
StepFrontier (node: g)Expand
1Arad:0Arad
2Zerind:75, Timișoara:118, Sibiu:140Zerind
………
k…, Bucharest:418, …Bucharest when it is the lowest
formula: g = exact path cost from the start
when the goal is selected (popped), not when generated
example: From Arad: Zerind 75, Timișoara 118, Sibiu 140 → expand Zerind first (75).
Bucharest is returned with f = g = 418.
cards.trap: Do not stop when Bucharest is first ADDED to the frontier (via Făgăraș, 450); wait until it is popped with the lowest cost (418).

cards.title: Greedy best-first search
cards.hook: Greedy runs toward whatever LOOKS closest to the goal and ignores the cost already paid.
cards.visual:
From Aradh(n) = SLD to Bucharest
Sibiu253 ← pick
Timișoara329
Zerind374
then Făgăraș176 ← pick (vs RV 193, Oradea 380)
formula: estimated cost from n to the goal
Not always (graph version on finite spaces: yes)
example: Node A (g=400, h=50) vs node B (g=100, h=80): greedy picks h = 50, ignoring g.
cards.trap: Greedy reaches Bucharest via Făgăraș (cost 450), not the optimal 418.

cards.title: A* search
cards.hook: A* balances what you've spent (g) with what you still expect to spend (h).
formula: estimated cost of the cheapest path through n
path cost from start to n
estimated cost from n to goal
cards.memory: UCS looks Back, Greedy looks Forward, A* looks Both ways.
cards.trap: Compare f against EVERY frontier node (e.g. Timișoara 447 is still waiting), not just the newest children.

cards.title: Admissible vs consistent heuristics
cards.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 150" class="gsvg"><line x1="40" y1="120" x2="150" y2="30" class="ge"/><line x1="150" y1="30" x2="260" y2="120" class="ge"/><line x1="40" y1="120" x2="260" y2="120" class="ge" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/><circle cx="40" cy="120" r="14" class="gn"/><text x="40" y="124" class="gl">n</text><circle cx="150" cy="30" r="14" class="gn"/><text x="150" y="34" class="gl">n′</text><circle cx="260" cy="120" r="14" class="gn goal"/><text x="260" y="124" class="gl">G</text><text x="80" y="65" class="gw">c(n,a,n′)</text><text x="225" y="65" class="gw">h(n′)</text><text x="150" y="140" class="gw">h(n) ≤ c + h(n′)</text></svg>
cards.hook: A* is only guaranteed optimal if the heuristic is honest about remaining cost.
formula: h(n) ≤ c(n,a,n′) + h(n′) for every successor
tree-search A*: admissible h; graph-search A*: consistent h
example: SLD is admissible: a straight line is never longer than a road route.
If h(A) = 10, c(A,B) = 2, h(B) = 5: 10 > 2 + 5 → NOT consistent at edge A→B.
cards.memory: Admissible = optimistic. Consistent = optimistic at every single step.
cards.trap: 'Admissible' and 'consistent' are swapped in exam traps: consistency is the STRONGER property.

cheat.title: Classical Search cheat sheet
traps: Goal test on SELECTION for UCS/A*: don't stop when the goal is merely generated.
Ties: follow the stated tie-break (alphabetical here).
Greedy ignores g; UCS ignores h.
Repeated states: graph search skips explored states.
